deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding folios (four-term theta products with arguments n+p+r+d+f etc., the substitution x+y+z+t=2x', x+y-z-t=2y', ..., and counts of even/odd characteristics for p=3,4) concern Riemann's quartic theta relation. This page is a sketch of a proof of that relation by transformation (multiplier) arguments. Riemann's normalisation is assumed throughout: theta(v) = sum over m in Z^n of exp(sum a_{mu,nu} m_mu m_nu + 2 sum m_mu v_mu). The periods are pi*i*e_mu and the columns a_{.,mu}; the half-periods are pi*i/2 and a_{.,mu}/2.

(1) Top lines. He writes the product of four thetas at the Hadamard-transformed arguments, with each argument shifted by a period epsilon*pi*i and a sign (-1)^{eps eps'}: theta(x+y+z+t+eps*pi*i) * theta(x+y-z-t+eps*pi*i) * theta(x-y-z+t+eps*pi*i) * theta(x-y+z-t+eps*pi*i). In n variables he sums Sigma (-1)^{eps_1 eps_1'+...+eps_n eps_n'} theta*theta*theta*theta. This is the shape of the left side of Riemann's theta formula, summed over characteristics with character signs.

(2) One-variable multiplier bookkeeping (left middle column). He tabulates argument, period shift and resulting exponential factor.
- '2x, 2a_{11}, -4(2x_1+a_{11})': theta(v+2a) = exp(-4v-4a) theta(v). With v=2x (i.e. x -> x+a), the factor is exp(-4(2x_1+a_{11})).
- '2x, a_{11}, -2(2x_1)(+/-)a_{11}+eps*pi*i': the half-step x -> x+a/2 gives exp(-2(2x_1)-a_{11}). The sign (-1)^eps = exp(eps*pi*i) appears when a characteristic is present.
- 'e^{4x_1^2/a_{11}}': the compensating factor. 4(x_1+a_{11})^2/a_{11} - 4x_1^2/a_{11} = 4(2x_1+a_{11}), which exactly cancels the theta multiplier.
Equivalently, take the four arguments x+-y+-z+-t and shift x by a: each theta contributes exp(-2 arg_1 - a_{11}). The product contributes exp(-8x_1-4a_{11}) = exp(-4(2x_1+a_{11})), cancelled by exp(4x_1^2/a_{11}).

(3) n-variable version (right column). He introduces the adjugate alpha_{nu,nu'} of the period matrix: Sigma_nu alpha_{nu,nu'} a_{mu,nu} = 0 for mu != nu' and = lambda (the determinant) for mu = nu'. So alpha/lambda = a^{-1}. Set Q(x) = Sigma alpha_{nu,nu'} x_nu x_nu'/lambda = x^T a^{-1} x. Then:
- Q(x + a_{1,.}) = Q(x) + 2x_1 + a_{11}. This matches the jottings '4(2x_1+a_{11})', 'x_nu + a_{1,nu}', '2x lambda + ... + (1/4)Sigma alpha a_{1nu} a_{1nu'}', '+(1/4) lambda a_{11}'.
- For the half-period, Q(x + (1/2) eps'_mu a_{.,mu}) = Q(x) + eps'_mu x_mu + (1/4) a_{mu mu} eps'_mu^2. This is the jotting 'eps'_mu y_mu + (1/4) a_{mu,mu} eps'_mu^2' (written in the variable y).
Hence exp(4Q(x)) exactly absorbs the multiplier of the four-fold product under the a-periods.

(4) Final formulas. He first uses only pi*i/2 shifts with the diagonal factors exp(4 Sigma x_mu^2/a_mu_mu + 4 Sigma y_mu^2/a_mu_mu + ...). This is a struck/abandoned diagonal attempt. He then writes the general expression
Sigma_{eps,eps'} (-1)^{eps.eta + eps'.eta'} Prod_{4 args} theta(v_mu + eps_mu*pi*i/2 + (1/2) Sigma_nu eps'_nu a_{mu,nu}, ...) * exp(4Q(x) + 4Q(y) + 4Q(z) + 4Q(t)) = f(eta_1..eta_n, eta'_1..eta'_n).
Unstated but evidently intended (mine): Q(x+y+z+t)+Q(x+y-z-t)+Q(x-y-z+t)+Q(x-y+z-t) = 4(Q(x)+Q(y)+Q(z)+Q(t)), because the transformation is orthogonal up to the factor 2. So the exponential factor can be written in either set of variables. The character sum over half-period translates then projects onto a combination depending only on the characteristic (eta, eta'). That is the standard route to Riemann's formula Sigma (-1)^{...} Prod theta[...] = 2^n Prod theta[...](x)theta(y)theta(z)theta(t). The page stops at naming the result f(eta, eta').
errors: No genuine mathematical errors are detectable. The page is fragmentary bookkeeping, and the multiplier computations that can be checked are correct.
The sign before a_{1,1} in '-2(2x_1) ... a_{1,1}' should be minus for the half-step x -> x+a/2. The machine transcription's '+' is probably a misreading.

The claim '= f(eta,eta')' (independence of the variables) is not justified on the page. The exp(4Q) factor restores a-periodicity but destroys pi*i-periodicity, so a further argument is needed. It is only sketched.
The first line uses full-period shifts eps*pi*i (under which theta is invariant). The later lines correctly switch to half-periods eps*pi*i/2 and eps'*a/2.

results.what: Product of four thetas at Hadamard-transformed arguments x+-y+-z+-t, summed over half-period characteristics with signs (-1)^{eps.eta+eps'.eta'}
results.modern_name: Riemann's theta formula (quartic addition theorem / Riemann's theta relation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published through Prym 1882 and later Krazer, from Riemann's lectures/notes)

results.what: Multiplier of theta under the a-period, theta(v+a_{.,mu}) = exp(-2v_mu - a_{mu mu}) theta(v), and its compensation by exp(4 x^T a^{-1} x)
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity of theta functions; normalisation by a quadratic exponential (factor of automorphy)

results.what: Q(x+a e_mu) = Q(x)+2x_mu+a_{mu mu} and Q(x+a e_mu/2) = Q(x)+x_mu+a_{mu mu}/4 for Q = x^T a^{-1} x, using the adjugate alpha and determinant lambda

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's theta formula is already attributed to Riemann. This page is working bookkeeping (multipliers, quadratic compensating factors, character sums) towards its proof. It is a mildly interesting glimpse of his proof method, but nothing new.

checkable.asserts: The Hadamard substitution scales the quadratic form by 4, so the exponential factor is the same in old and new variables.
The factor e^{4x^2/a} picks up e^{4(2x+a)} under x -> x+a.
The product of four thetas whose arguments each shift by a has multiplier exp(-4(2x_1+a)), cancelling the previous factor.
Termwise reindexing m -> m+1 proves theta(v+a) = exp(-2v-a) theta(v) in Riemann's normalisation.
The half-period shift changes Q by x_mu + a_{mu mu}/4 (the jotting eps'_mu y_mu + 1/4 a_{mu mu} eps'^2).
A pi*i/2 shift introduces the sign (-1)^m, i.e. it changes the characteristic.

transcription_corrections: Lines '2x 2a_{1,1}' and '2x -4(2x_1+a_{1,1})' form a table (argument, period shift, multiplier) for theta(2x) under x -> x+a. They are not independent formulas.
'-2(2x_1)+a_{1,1}+eps pi i' is more likely '-2(2x_1)-a_{1,1}+eps pi i' (the multiplier for the half-step).
'Sigma alpha_{nu,nu'} a_{mu,nu} = 0, nu' <> 1' should read: = 0 for mu != nu' (adjugate relation), and Sigma alpha_{nu,1} a_{1,nu} = lambda (determinant).
The struck exponent before '+4 Sigma y_mu^2/a_mu_mu' began with '4 Sigma x_mu^2/a_mu_mu' (the diagonal version).
The right side reads f(eta_1, eta_2, ..., eta_n, eta'_1, eta'_2, ..., eta'_n).
In the top line the shifts under each argument appear as '+eps_1 pi i' (index possibly nu). The fourth argument is x-y+z-t, written without subscripts.
